note: Read for two things, neither a surface. (1) Prairie Avenue was not a South Park boulevard in 1897: the code's boulevards are Michigan Avenue, 35th Street, Grand, Drexel, Oakwood, Garfield and the Midway, and 'Prairie' appears in it only as a landmark for an elevated railroad's alignment. (2) Streetcars ran on two of the 1904 grid's streets: in 1896 the Chicago City Railway had 'in operation on Indiana avenue ... and on Eighteenth street ... a double track street railway, by horse cars, which it desires to change to electric power ... by means of the overhead trolley' (pp. 241-242). The code shows only where those lines crossed the Commissioners' boulevards; how far along Indiana Avenue and 18th Street the tracks ran, and on what paving, it does not say. The tracks are not drawn in the 1904 scene (docs/LIBERTIES.md L295).
what_it_supplies: that Prairie Avenue was not among the South Park Commissioners' boulevards in 1897
that the Chicago City Railway ran a double-track line on Indiana Avenue and on 18th Street in 1896, by horse cars, with electric traction being sought
what_it_does_not_supply: the extent of either line within the 1904 grid, or its state in 1904
any roadway surface of the grid
